- `two-chapters.epub`: a two-chapter EPUB 3 of our own text with a two-entry nav TOC; chapter two carries an inline `<script>`, `onload` and `onclick` handlers, and an external script resource `scripts/marker.js` that would each insert a marker paragraph if they ran. Chapter one ends with a paragraph (`id="links"`) of links out of the book (`https:`, `mailto:`, a `javascript:` href that would insert a `ran-link` marker, `data:`) and one link to chapter two.
- `two-chapters.mobi`, `two-chapters.azw3`: two chapters of our own text ("One: The Lighthouse Ledger", "Two: The Unsent Letters"). Chapter two carries an inline `<script>` and an `<img onload>` handler that would each insert a marker paragraph (`ran-inline`, `ran-handler`) if they ran. Made from one HTML file with `ebook-convert two-chapters.html two-chapters.azw3 --title "Two Chapters" --authors "Calibre Cloud" --level1-toc "//h:h1" --chapter "//h:h1" --chapter-mark pagebreak`. Calibre's old-MOBI writer drops scripts and `on*` attributes, so the MOBI is built with `--mobi-file-type old --dont-compress` from the same HTML with a placeholder paragraph (`<p>SCRIPTSLOT___…</p>`) in place of the image and script; the placeholder's bytes in the uncompressed text are then overwritten with the `<img onload>` and `<script>` markup, space-padded to the same length so no record or `filepos` offset moves.
- `two-chapters.fb2`: the same two chapters, hand-written as two titled `<section>`s. `two-chapters.fbz` is that file zipped.
- `two-pages.cbz`: two 300×400 PNG pages, `page-1.png` (red) and `page-2.png` (blue), each labelled with its name.
- `two-fixed-pages.epub`: a two-page fixed-layout (`rendition:layout` `pre-paginated`) EPUB 3 of our own text, 300×400 per page, with a two-entry nav TOC ("Page one", "Page two").
- `one-file-two-chapters.epub`: an EPUB 3 of our own text whose one spine file holds both chapters ("One: The Keeper", "Two: The Visitor"), with a nav TOC that points at each by fragment. "lamp" appears twice in chapter one and once in chapter two. Made with Python's `zipfile`, `mimetype` stored first.
- `two-pages.pdf`: two pages of our own text with a two-entry outline ("Page one", "Page two"), for the PDF renderer test.
